newsitem.title: CANADA: Prairie farmers to be briefed on flood risk - CWB.
newsitem.headline: Prairie farmers to be briefed on flood risk - CWB.

text.p: Farmers in Canada's eastern Prairies will be briefed Tuesday and Wednesday by weather and transportation experts on flood potential and grain movement prior to spring thaw, a Canadian Wheat Board statement said.
Farmers will be briefed by officials from CWB, Environment Canada, Manitoba Agriculture, Manitoba Highways and Transportation and Manitoba Natural Resources, it said.
Snowfall in the Red River watershed, which includes much of Minnesota and North Dakota, is twice to three times the normal amount, Manitoba Water Resources Branch manager Rick Bowering has said.
Soils were saturated at freeze-up last fall and are unlikely to absorb water during spring thaw, Bowering said.
The potential for spring flooding along the Red River is the second highest since 1950.
The 1950 flood was the worst in Manitoba in this century when much of Winnipeg was underwater. A peripheral drainage ditch was since built around the city to handle high floods.
The Winnipeg, Whitemouth, Brokenhead and Whiteshell rivers also have high flood potentials, MWRB has said.
Assiniboine and Souris river watersheds may flood on above average precipitation between now and April, MWRB has said.
